5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine congratulated the Montrose Shopping Park Association for a
  successful and well-attended event of their 39th Anniversary of the Arts and Crafts Festival.
  She also commended the Glendale Rotary for a successful Cars for Cops Event held at
  Verdugo Park.

  Councilmember Asatryan thanked staff for coordinating the Small Business Summit Week.
  She was glad about the turnout and enjoyed seeing diversity in the group. Asatryan thanked
  Supervisor Katherine Barger and the Small Business Administration for sponsoring the
  event. Since council did not have a meeting last week in celebration of the Memorial Day
  Holiday, Asatryan acknowledged the veterans who sacrificed their lives so we can all be
  here today. She stated that Memorial Day is not only to thank our veterans, but also for the
  city to push for policies to support veterans and their families that are struggling.

  Asatryan asked Police Chief Cid to provide a brief update regarding the protest on the street
  that was taking place during the council meeting. Cid reported the protest is regarding the
  Glendale Unified School Board Meeting on Proclaiming June 2023 as LGBTQ+ Pride Month.
  He indicated that police officers have made a few arrests and an order is in place. Chief Cid
  talked about the successful Gun Buy Back Program held last Saturday.

  Councilmember Kassakhian thanked the Glendale Police Department for keeping the
  community safe and stated he is disheartened to see the public acting uncivilized. He
  thanked council for recognizing the month of June as Pride Month. Kassakhian attended the
  3
   Independence Day Celebration for Armenia on May 28 at Parcher Plaza and congratulated
  the organizers of the event. He also congratulated students who will graduate this month.

  Mayor Brotman indicated that the three-minute portion of the Community Events
  Announcement will now be only reserved for public event announcements and public
  comments will be heard by council at the five-minute portion of the Oral Communications or
  during specific agenda items. Brotman asked council to address a trend on “dangerous and
  divisive speech,” which targets many community members such as Armenians, Asian-
  Americans and Pacific Islanders, Jews, and LGBTQ population. Kassakhian seconded.
  Brotman stated that the Jewish Federation of the Greater San Gabriel and Pomona Valley
  asked council to consider adopting a Resolution against Anti-Semitism. Mayor Brotman
  gave kudos to Public Works for implementing “Leading Pedestrian Intervals,” an opportunity
  for pedestrians to enter the crosswalk at an intersection a few seconds before vehicles are
  given a green indication. He asked council to adjourn the council meeting in memory of
  Chad Edginton, Principal Power System Operator of GWP.
